nodes.name: PVP-stabilized Cu(0) NP synthesis
nodes.procedure: PVP-coated Cu(0) NPs were readily prepared by a conventional chemical reduction route.
nodes.source_text: PVP-coated Cu(0) NPs were readily prepared by a conventional chemical reduction route

nodes.name: PEG-stabilized transition metal NP synthesis
nodes.procedure: Astruc's group prepared a tris(triazolyl) fragment-functionalized PEG-2000 ligand and utilized it as stabilizer in syntheses of Fe NPs, Co NPs, Ni NPs, and Cu NPs with very small particle size ranging from 1.3 to 2.1 nm.
nodes.source_text: Astruc's group prepared a tris(triazolyl) fragment-functionalized PEG-2000 ligand and utilized it as stabilizer in syntheses of Fe NPs, Co NPs, Ni NPs, and Cu NPs

nodes.name: PAMAM-encapsulated Co NP synthesis
nodes.procedure: The complexation of hydroxyl-terminated PAMAM dendrimers of generation 6 (G6) with Co2+ cations, and further reduction by both ammonia borane (AB) and NaBH4 were carried out, and the assembly of PAMAM-encapsulated Co NPs (G6-OH(Co60)) was achieved using this process.
nodes.source_text: The complexation of hydroxyl-terminated PAMAM dendrimers of generation 6 (G6) with Co2+ cations, and further reduction by both ammonia borane (AB) and NaBH4

nodes.name: Microwave-assisted Fe3O4 NP synthesis
nodes.procedure: Fe3O4 NPs with an average size of 6 nm generated in situ from Fe(acac)3 using hydrazine hydrate as reductant using small-scale microwave batch heating at 150°C.
nodes.source_text: Kappe's group generated Fe3O4 NPs with an average size of 6 nm in situ from Fe(acac)3 using hydrazine hydrate as reductant using a small-scale microwave batch heating at 150°C

nodes.name: Photogeneration of Ni(0) NPs
nodes.procedure: Reduction of NiCl2 to Ni(0) NPs efficiently driven by visible light in the presence of fluorescein and in basic aqueous solution.
nodes.source_text: The reduction of NiCl2 to Ni(0) NPs was efficiently driven by visible light in the presence of fluorescein and in basic aqueous solution

nodes.name: Mechanochemical Ni NPs in MgH2
nodes.procedure: Yao's group reported a one-step fabrication of 2–3 nm Ni NPs in a MgH2 matrix through a mechanochemical-force-driven approach, starting from a Ni-based MOF, with the use of MgH2 as a reducing and sacrificial agent.
nodes.source_text: one-step fabrication of 2–3 nm Ni NPs in a MgH2 matrix through a mechanochemical-force-driven approach

nodes.name: Microemulsion synthesis of Ni NPs in heavy oil
nodes.procedure: Ultra-dispersed Ni NPs (22±5 nm) in heavy oil (20 wt% vacuum residue, 80 wt% vacuum gas oil) prepared using water-in-oil microemulsion protocol with aqueous Ni(NO3)2 and hydrazine as precursor and reductant.
nodes.source_text: Husein et al. successfully prepared ultra-dispersed Ni NPs in heavy oil composed of 20 wt% vacuum residue and 80 wt% vacuum gas oil using a water-in-oil microemulsion protocol

nodes.name: Thermal synthesis of Mn3O4 NPs
nodes.procedure: Mn3O4 NPs simply synthesized by thermal treatment of MnCl2·4H2O or Mn(OAc)2·4H2O.
nodes.source_text: Mn3O4 NPs were also simply synthesized by thermal treatment of MnCl2·4H2O or Mn(OAc)2·4H2O

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu NPs stabilized by PEG, CMC, and PVP have mean sizes of 6 nm, 12 nm, and 15 nm respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Parimala et al. reported that Cu NPs were successfully assembled using PEG, CMC and PVP as stabilizers under the same conditions with mean sizes of 6, 12 and 15 nm, respectively.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The pre-synthesized G6-OH(Co60) with an average diameter of 1.6 nm has been shown to be a high-performance catalyst.
